source.text: Ἐνετειλάμην σοι, φησίν, ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ ἐντολῇ ἵνα φυλάξῃς τὴν πίστιν καὶ τὸν φόβον καὶ τὴν ἐγκράτειαν. Ναί, φημί, κύριε. Ἀλλὰ νῦν θέλω σοι, φησί, δηλῶσαι καὶ τὰς δυνάμεις αὐτῶν, ἵνα νοήσῃς τίς αὐτῶν τίνα δύναμιν ἔχει καὶ ἐνέργειαν. διπλαῖ γάρ εἰσιν αἱ ἐνέργειαι αὐτῶν· κεῖνται οὖν ἐπὶ δικαίῳ καὶ ἀδίκῳ· 2. σὺ οὖν πίστευε τῷ δικαίῳ, τῷ δὲ ἀδίκῳ μὴ πιστεύσῃς· τὸ γὰρ δίκαιον ὀρθὴν ὁδὸν ἔχει, τὸ δὲ ἄδικον στρεβλήν. ἀλλὰ σὺ τῇ ὀρθῇ ὁδῷ πορεύου [καὶ ὁμαλῇ], τὴν δὲ στρεβλὴν ἔασον. 3. ἡ γὰρ στρεβλὴ ὁδὸς τρίβους οὐκ ἔχει, ἀλλ᾽ ἀνοδίας καὶ προσκόμματα πολλά, καὶ τραχεῖά ἐστι καὶ ἀκανθώδης. βλαβερὰ οὖν ἐστὶ τοῖς σοί τις προσπέσῃ ἡ πικρία, γίνωσκε ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ἐν σοί· εἶτα ἐπιθυμία πράξεων πολλῶν καὶ πολυτέλεια ἐδεσμάτων πολλῶν καὶ μεθυσμάτων καὶ κραιπαλῶν πολλῶν καὶ ποικίλων τρυφῶν καὶ οὐ δεόντων, καὶ ἐπιθυμία γυναικῶν καὶ πλεονεξία καὶ ὑπερηφανία καὶ ἀλαζονεία, καὶ ὅσα τούτοις παραπλήσιά ἐστι καὶ ὅμοια. ταῦτα οὖν ὅταν ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, γίνωσκε ὅτι ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς πονηρίας ἐστὶ μετὰ σοῦ. 6. σὺ οὖν ἐπιγνοὺς τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἀπόστα ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ καὶ μηδὲν αὐτῷ πίστευε, ὅτι τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρά εἰσι καὶ ἀσύμφορα τοῖς δούλοις τοῦ Θεοῦ. ἔχεις οὖν ἀμφοτέρων τῶν ἀγγέλων τὰς ἐνεργείας· σύνιε αὐτὰς καὶ πίστευε τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς δικαιοσύνης· 7. ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς πονηρίας ἀπόστηθι, ὅτι ἡ διδαχὴ αὐτοῦ πονηρά ἐστι παντὶ ἔργῳ· ἐὰν γὰρ ᾖ τις πιστὸς ἀνήρ, καὶ ἡ ἐνθύμησις τοῦ ἀγγέλου τούτου ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ, δεῖ τὸν ἄνδρα ἐκεῖνον ἢ τὴν γυναῖκα ἐξαμαρτῆσαί τι. 8. ἐὰν δὲ πάλιν πονηρότατός τις ᾖ ἀνὴρ ἢ γυνή, καὶ ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης, ἐξ ἀνάγκης δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀγαθον τι ποιῆσαι. 9. βλέπεις οὖν, φησίν, ὅτι καλόν ἐστι τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἀκολουθεῖν, τῷ δὲ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς πονηρίας ἀποτάξασθαι. 10. τὰ μὲν περὶ τῆς πίστεως αὕτη ἡ ἐντολὴ δηλοῖ, ἵνα τοῖς ἔργοις τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης πιστεύσῃς, καὶ ἐργασάμενος αὐτὰ ζήσῃ τῷ Θεῷ. πίστευε δὲ ὅτι τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς πονηρίας χαλεπά ἐστι· μὴ ἐργαζόμενος οὖν αὐτὰ ζήσῃ τῷ Θεῷ.

translation.text:
He says[1], “I commanded you in the first commandment to keep faith and fear and self-control.”[2] “Yes, lord,” I say. “But now,” he says, “I also want to make known to you their powers, so that you may understand what power and activity each of them has. For their activities are twofold; so they have to do with what is righteous and what is unrighteous. So you—trust what is righteous, but do not trust what is unrighteous; for what is righteous has a straight road, but what is unrighteous a crooked one. But you, walk on the straight [and level][1] road, and leave the crooked[2].

For the crooked path has no tracks, but pathless places and many stumbling blocks; and it is rough and thorny. Therefore it is harmful. But hear also the works of the other way. First of all, if there should come upon you a quick temper or bitterness, know that he is in you. Then come craving for many undertakings, and extravagance in many foods, and intoxicants and many revelries, and luxuries of various kinds, and things that are not fitting; and desire for women, and greed, and haughtiness, and boastfulness, and whatever things are akin and similar to these. Therefore, whenever these things rise up in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is with you.

So when you recognize his works, withdraw from him and put no trust in him, because his works are wicked and harmful to God’s servants. You therefore have the activities of both angels; discern them, and trust the angel of righteousness. But withdraw from the angel of wickedness, because his teaching is wicked in every deed. For if someone is a faithful man, and the thought of this angel rises up in his heart, that man or woman must commit some sin. But if again some man or woman is very wicked, and the works of the angel of righteousness rise up in his or her heart, that person must of necessity do something good. You see then,” he says, “that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness, and to renounce the angel of wickedness. As to faith, this commandment makes it clear: that you should trust the works of the angel of righteousness, and, having done them, live to God.[3] But believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are grievous; so by not doing them[a][3], you will live to God.”

footnotes.text: Some witnesses include 'and level' (καὶ ὁμαλῇ) after 'straight.'
The 'first commandment' alludes back to the opening mandate where foundational virtues are given.
'Trust the works' reflects πιστεύειν with a dative; alternatives include 'give credence to' or 'heed.'
Or 'and pleasures of various kinds that are not fitting'.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Default rendering per project policy; here it names a virtue to be guarded alongside fear and self-control.
Moral-exhortation context; concise and weighty. The object is implicitly God.
Standard moral virtue; contemporary and clear without archaic tone.
Refers to the effective capacity of the virtues; preserves concrete sense.
Describes what they effect/do; 'activities' is natural English and avoids metaphysical overtones of 'energies'.
Moral-spiritual frame throughout the unit; 'righteous' pairs with 'angel of righteousness' later.
Maintains symmetry with 'righteous' and moral nuance, not merely legal injustice.
Concrete road imagery; 'crooked' captures στρεβλή's moral-twisted connotation.
Footpath nuance fits the road metaphor; 'tracks' contrasts with 'trackless' below.
Conveys absence of usable roads; keeps the metaphor vivid.
Common moral metaphor; concrete and idiomatic.
Plain English for uneven, harsh terrain.
Natural, vivid description; keeps the concrete image.
Standard ethical term; suits inner sourness linked to wicked influence.
Here of appetitive urge; 'craving' fits vices list tone.
Here the context is restless busyness; 'undertakings' implies many pursuits.
Conveys excess rather than mere quality; matches vice catalog.
'Foods' is clear and broad; 'dishes/viands' is archaic.
Specifies alcoholic drinks with intoxicating effect; succinct and precise.
'Revelries' captures feasting/riotous excess without archaic or moralistic inflation.
In a vice list, 'luxuries' concisely names soft-living indulgence.
Plain English; moral impropriety without formality.
Modern equivalent; 'covetousness' is accurate but archaic in tone.
Highlights disdainful superiority, distinct from ἀλαζονεία.
Self-exalting display; 'boastfulness' pairs well with 'haughtiness'.
Inner consideration/impulse arising in the heart; 'thought' keeps idiomatic clarity.
Transparently expresses moral failure; indefinite 'some' reflects τι.
Idiomatic for decisive parting; moral break with the wicked angel.
Neutral term; context supplies moral evaluation.
Common early-Christian idiom for spiritually unhelpful; fits contrast with 'live to God'.
Per project policy, 'slaves' when bonded belonging is salient; here opposed to another lord’s works.
Carries the sense of hard/cruel; 'grievous' suits moral weight.
Moral discernment is in view; 'discern' fits evaluative context.
Imperative of spatial/moral separation; 'withdraw' is vivid and brief.
With personal object and even with 'works', 'trust' best conveys allegiance/credence in moral instruction.
Standard moral metaphor of discipleship/path.
Preserves dative idiom familiar in early Christian diction; noted in theological decisions.

theological_decisions.issue: Genitive titles for angels (τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης / τῆς πονηρίας)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render as 'angel of righteousness' / 'angel of wickedness'
theological_decisions.rationale: The genitive denotes the moral quality these angels represent or administer; preserving it keeps Hermas’s moral taxonomy explicit.
Per project policy, 'slave' highlights belonging and allegiance; here contrasted with trusting the wicked angel’s works.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: Translation philosophy: contested terms — doulos → slave where bonded nature salient.

theological_decisions.rationale: The dative expresses orientation; 'to God' preserves early Christian idiom and rhetorical symmetry within the mandate.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render 'trust' rather than 'believe' when the object is a person or 'works'
theological_decisions.rationale: 'Trust' fits allegiance/credence; 'believe the works' is awkward in English while 'trust' is idiomatic and maintains the exhortational force.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render 'faithful person' (inclusive of man or woman by following clause)
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas immediately includes 'that man or that woman'; 'faithful person' captures moral-religious status without gender restriction.

theological_decisions.issue: Internal moral influence phrased as 'he is in you'
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Translate literally to preserve Hermas’s moral-psychological imagery
alternative_readings: he is at work in you
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas depicts the presence of either angel in the heart via arising thoughts; retaining 'in you' keeps the vivid interior imagery.

review_passes.summary: The draft is generally strong, but misinterprets 'κεῖνται ἐπὶ δικαίῳ καὶ ἀδίκῳ' as referring to people ('the righteous and the unrighteous') rather than the concepts of right and wrong (neuter). Several instances of 'οὖν' are omitted, and there is a minor inconsistency in translating 'ἀφίστημι'. The revised text corrects these issues to better reflect the author's precise moral categories and logical flow.
issues_found: Mistranslation: 'κεῖνται οὖν ἐπὶ δικαίῳ καὶ ἀδίκῳ' is rendered 'they lie upon both the righteous and the unrighteous.' BDAG explicitly cites this verse for 'κεῖμαι ἐπὶ' meaning 'have to do with.' Furthermore, 'δικαίῳ' and 'ἀδίκῳ' are neuter here (as confirmed by 'τὸ γὰρ δίκαιον' in the next clause), not masculine. The draft also misses 'οὖν'.

Lexical choice: 'τῷ δικαίῳ, τῷ δὲ ἀδίκῳ' is rendered 'the righteous... the unrighteous,' which sounds like people. It should be 'what is righteous... what is unrighteous' to match the neuter adjectives and the explanatory clause that follows.
Missing nuance: 'ταῦτα οὖν ὅταν' misses the translation of 'οὖν' (Therefore).
Consistency: 'ἀπόστηθι' is rendered 'take your distance from,' but the same verb (ἀφίστημι) is translated 'withdraw from' in the preceding verse. Consistency strengthens the rhetorical repetition.
Lexical choice: 'πίστευε δὲ ὅτι' is rendered 'And be convinced that,' but 'πίστευε' is the same verb translated 'trust' throughout the passage, and 'δὲ' is 'but.' 'But believe that' is more accurate.
Missing nuance: 'μὴ ἐργαζόμενος οὖν αὐτὰ' misses the translation of 'οὖν' (so/therefore).

revisions.from: and pleasures of various kinds that are not fitting
revisions.to: and luxuries of various kinds, and things that are not fitting
revisions.rationale: The Greek 'καὶ ποικίλων τρυφῶν καὶ οὐ δεόντων' contains two distinct genitive items. 'δεόντων' is neuter plural ('things not fitting') and stands as its own substantive in the list, rather than modifying the feminine 'τρυφῶν'. Additionally, the project's lexical decision for τρυφῶν is 'luxuries', not 'pleasures'. | Adjudicator: The reviewer is grammatically correct. In the Greek phrase 'καὶ ποικίλων τρυφῶν καὶ οὐ δεόντων', 'τρυφῶν' is a feminine noun (genitive plural) while 'δεόντων' is a neuter participle (genitive plural).

revisions.rationale: Improved lexical accuracy and completeness: rendered κεῖνται as “are set over,” δικαίῳ/ἀδίκῳ as “the righteous/the unrighteous,” and ὁδός as “path” consistently in the road metaphor. Restored omitted material after “Therefore it is harmful” (“But hear also the works of the other way. First of all... quick temper”), and adjusted several vice terms for closer sense (e.g., “drinks,” “drunken sprees,” “arrogance”). Smoothed English while keeping a formal register.

source.text: Ἐνετειλάμην σοι, φησίν, ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ ἐντολῇ ἵνα φυλάξῃς τὴν πίστιν καὶ τὸν φόβον καὶ τὴν ἐγκράτειαν. Ναί, φημί, κύριε. Ἀλλὰ νῦν θέλω σοι, φησί, δηλῶσαι καὶ τὰς δυνάμεις αὐτῶν, ἵνα νοήσῃς τίς αὐτῶν τίνα δύναμιν ἔχει καὶ ἐνέργειαν. διπλαῖ γάρ εἰσιν αἱ ἐνέργειαι αὐτῶν· κεῖνται οὖν ἐπὶ δικαίῳ καὶ ἀδίκῳ· 2. σὺ οὖν πίστευε τῷ δικαίῳ, τῷ δὲ ἀδίκῳ μὴ πιστεύσῃς· τὸ γὰρ δίκαιον ὀρθὴν ὁδὸν ἔχει, τὸ δὲ ἄδικον στρεβλήν. ἀλλὰ σὺ τῇ ὀρθῇ ὁδῷ πορεύου [καὶ ὁμαλῇ], τὴν δὲ στρεβλὴν ἔασον. 3. ἡ γὰρ στρεβλὴ ὁδὸς τρίβους οὐκ ἔχει, ἀλλ᾽ ἀνοδίας καὶ προσκόμματα πολλά, καὶ τραχεῖά ἐστι καὶ ἀκανθώδης. βλαβερὰ οὖν ἐστὶ τοῖς σοί τις προσπέσῃ ἡ πικρία, γίνωσκε ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ἐν σοί· εἶτα ἐπιθυμία πράξεων πολλῶν καὶ πολυτέλεια ἐδεσμάτων πολλῶν καὶ μεθυσμάτων καὶ κραιπαλῶν πολλῶν καὶ ποικίλων τρυφῶν καὶ οὐ δεόντων, καὶ ἐπιθυμία γυναικῶν καὶ πλεονεξία καὶ ὑπερηφανία καὶ ἀλαζονεία, καὶ ὅσα τούτοις παραπλήσιά ἐστι καὶ ὅμοια. ταῦτα οὖν ὅταν ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, γίνωσκε ὅτι ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς πονηρίας ἐστὶ μετὰ σοῦ. 6. σὺ οὖν ἐπιγνοὺς τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἀπόστα ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ καὶ μηδὲν αὐτῷ πίστευε, ὅτι τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρά εἰσι καὶ ἀσύμφορα τοῖς δούλοις τοῦ Θεοῦ. ἔχεις οὖν ἀμφοτέρων τῶν ἀγγέλων τὰς ἐνεργείας· σύνιε αὐτὰς καὶ πίστευε τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς δικαιοσύνης· 7. ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς πονηρίας ἀπόστηθι, ὅτι ἡ διδαχὴ αὐτοῦ πονηρά ἐστι παντὶ ἔργῳ· ἐὰν γὰρ ᾖ τις πιστὸς ἀνήρ, καὶ ἡ ἐνθύμησις τοῦ ἀγγέλου τούτου ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ, δεῖ τὸν ἄνδρα ἐκεῖνον ἢ τὴν γυναῖκα ἐξαμαρτῆσαί τι. 8. ἐὰν δὲ πάλιν πονηρότατός τις ᾖ ἀνὴρ ἢ γυνή, καὶ ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης, ἐξ ἀνάγκης δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀγαθον τι ποιῆσαι. 9. βλέπεις οὖν, φησίν, ὅτι καλόν ἐστι τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἀκολουθεῖν, τῷ δὲ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς πονηρίας ἀποτάξασθαι. 10. τὰ μὲν περὶ τῆς πίστεως αὕτη ἡ ἐντολὴ δηλοῖ, ἵνα τοῖς ἔργοις τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης πιστεύσῃς, καὶ ἐργασάμενος αὐτὰ ζήσῃ τῷ Θεῷ. πίστευε δὲ ὅτι τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς πονηρίας χαλεπά ἐστι· μὴ ἐργαζόμενος οὖν αὐτὰ ζήσῃ τῷ Θεῷ.

translation.text: For the crooked path has no tracks, but pathless places and many stumbling blocks; and it is rough and thorny. Therefore it is harmful. But hear also the works of the other way. First of all, if there should come upon you a quick temper or bitterness, know that he is in you. Then come desire for many activities, and extravagance in many foods and drinks, and many drunken sprees, and various luxuries, and things that are not fitting; and desire for women, and greed, and arrogance, and boastfulness, and whatever things are akin and similar to these. Therefore, whenever these things rise up in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is with you.

translation.text: So when you recognize his works, withdraw from him and put no trust in him, because his works are wicked and harmful to God’s servants. You therefore have the activities of both angels; understand them, and trust the angel of righteousness. But withdraw from the angel of wickedness, because his teaching is wicked in every deed. For if someone is a faithful man, and the thought of this angel rises up in his heart, that man or woman must commit some sin. But if again some man or woman is very wicked, and the works of the angel of righteousness rise up in his or her heart, that person must of necessity do something good. You see then,” he says, “that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness, and to renounce the angel of wickedness. As to faith, this commandment makes it clear: that you should trust the works of the angel of righteousness, and, having done them, live to God. But believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are grievous; so by not doing them, you will live to God.”

base_translation.text: He says, “I commanded you in the first commandment to keep faith and fear and self-control.” “Yes, lord,” I say. “But now,” he says, “I also want to make known to you their powers, so that you may understand what power and activity each of them has. For their activities are twofold; so they are set over the righteous and the unrighteous. So you—trust the righteous, but do not trust the unrighteous; for righteousness has a straight path, but unrighteousness a crooked one. But you, walk on the straight [and level] path, and leave the crooked.

translation.text:
He said, “In the first commandment, I told you to hold firmly to faith, fear, and self-control.”

“Yes, lord,” I replied.

“Now,” he said, “I also want to explain what power each one has and how each one works, so that you will understand. Their activities are twofold; so they are set over both the righteous and the unrighteous. Trust the righteous, but do not trust the unrighteous. Righteousness has a straight path, but unrighteousness has a crooked one. Walk on the straight [and level] path, and stay away from the crooked one.”

translation.text:
The crooked path has no clear tracks. It runs through trackless places and has many obstacles that make people stumble. It is rough and full of thorns, so it brings harm.

Now hear what the other way produces. First, if sudden anger or bitterness comes over you, know that the angel of wickedness is in you. Then come the desire to take on many activities, lavish eating and drinking, drunken parties, various luxuries and other improper things, lust for women, greed, arrogance, and boasting, along with everything else like them. translation.text:
“So when you recognize the angel of wickedness by what he does, turn away from him and do not trust him. His deeds are evil and harmful to God’s servants. Now you know how both angels act. Understand this, and trust the angel of righteousness. But turn away from the angel of wickedness, because his teaching is wicked in everything it leads people to do.

“Even if someone is faithful, when a thought from this angel enters that person’s heart, whether the person is a man or a woman, that person will inevitably commit some sin. On the other hand, even if someone is very wicked, when the works of the angel of righteousness arise in that person’s heart, that person will inevitably do something good.

“You see, then,” he says, “that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness and reject the angel of wickedness. This commandment makes clear what you should believe: trust the works of the angel of righteousness. Do them, and you will live for God. But believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are grievous. Refuse to do them, and you will live for God.”
